islands.law:
# The atlas's value wave, as a law of nature. Transcribed from Atlas._wave:
#
#     V = max(source, best neighbour * (1 - decay)^distance) * passable
#
# with decay 0.06 (0.94 per orthogonal step, 0.94^sqrt2 = 0.916214 per diagonal)
# and a solid cell letting `leak` of the wave through — the harness's per-cell
# leak, innate then taught per hue by what pressing on it did.
# max8 also contains the four orthogonal neighbours, but they are discounted
# more there than under max4, so the max of the two is exactly the eight-way
# wave with a diagonal that costs sqrt 2. The harness paints source and solid
# each thought, steps this `subticks` times, and reads value at the centre.

channel source
channel solid
channel value

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(source, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Confinement suppression (night lab 2026-09-23, champion #35): a source hemmed in by
# solid counts less, so local food in a nook stops dominating and the frontier wins there.
# 24.5 meals on 32 never-seen FINAL worlds vs 18.8 the reference wave, 17.1 the tuned ghost.

channel source
channel solid
channel free
channel thing
channel here
channel value
channel confinement
channel injection

# Measure local solidity to detect dead-ends/corridors.
# High sum8(solid) means tight space.
rule calc_conf:
  when 1
  set confinement = sum8(solid)

# Inject signals, but suppress heavily if in a tight space.
# The division by (1 + k*conf) reduces value in dead-ends.
# This prevents the agent from being pulled into local maxima in confined areas.
rule inject:
  when 1
  set injection = max(thing, source) / (1 + 0.5 * confinement)

# Propagate the value wave.
# Use standard Bellman decay. The suppressed injection ensures dead-ends don't dominate.
rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(injection, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

islands.law:
# Sources linger: a commitment law. The smell of a thing behind a wall is
# painted where the world's geodesic bearing points, and that bearing flips
# between the two ways round as the agent takes a step each way (seen on world
# 7: eleven frames out of twelve on the same spot, the source hopping left and
# right of it). Here a painted source keeps ~94% of itself per thought after
# the paint moves on, so the wave still holds the place it was first told and
# the nearer of the two stays the target. Where the agent stands there is
# nothing: `here` and its ring erase the ghost (an eaten morsel leaves no
# ghost to circle).

channel source
channel solid
channel here
channel value
channel ghost: init 0

rule linger:
  when 1
  set ghost = max(source, 0.99 * ghost) * (1 - here) * (1 - max8(here))

rule wave:
  when 1
  set value = max(ghost, max(0.94 * max4(value), 0.916214 * max8(value))) * (1 - solid * (1 - leak))

observations.text: The agent is born in a narrow sealed slot about one cell wide and four tall, walled by rock with patches of brown rubble right beside it, and it never leaves: the whole 4221-tick life is spent pacing up and down that slot (last 500 ticks in a 4x1 box) until it starves. It does try to dig — 11 breaks and 24 idle presses — but the presses are spread over different wall cells (much of it on plain rock), so no single rubble cell is ever chipped all the way through. The world outside is open and has food in reach (green spots above and to the left), so this is not a lack of food but a failure to commit to one exit. Confinement suppression makes it worse here: every source in a pocket is divided down, so the wave in the slot is weak and keeps re-pointing as the faint frontier/smell marks shift. The fix I would try first is a dig commitment: a per-cell memory that grows while the agent presses a solid cell and raises that cell's leak (its conductivity to the wave), so the wave keeps leading into the same rubble cell until it gives way instead of hopping between walls.

This world is a town of many small walled rooms with food scattered both outside and inside them; the agent lives the whole 8000 ticks, eats 13 times, and spends most of its life walking loop after loop around the OUTSIDE of room walls (the blue and red tracks trace room perimeters two and three times over). Food dots sit inside rooms whose walls it walks right along, yet it opens no door (doors 0) while pressing walls 42 times for nothing, so the wave is leading it into plain wall cells rather than the rooms' doors. Late in life (red) it is confined to one block of rooms in the upper right, circling the same corridors, so it is not starving for lack of food but for lack of a way in. The trail and frustration terms make walls it has lingered beside more conductive, which spreads the leak over whichever stone it happens to be next to, instead of the one cell that actually opens. The mechanism I would try is a thin-wall detector: a solid cell with free (or a seen thing) on both opposite sides is a door candidate and keeps its leak, while solid cells backed by more solid get almost none, so the wave pours through doorways and the presses land on doors.

turns.hypothesis: The confinement law has no memory: when the geodesic smell bearing flips between the two ways round a wall, its source hops and the agent oscillates (the trap the ghost law fixed), while the ghost law lacks confinement and is lured into nooks. Here a lingering ghost of every source (erased under the agent) is injected through the confinement divisor, and remembered refusals (`bad`) mute injection, so the target is both stable over time and discounted where it is hemmed in.

Exploration is a flat 0.12 on every frontier cell, so a crack into a one-cell pocket pulls as hard as an opening onto a wide unexplored region; most meals come from exploration, so the frontier should be worth what lies beyond it. This law keeps #3's lingering ghost + confinement, and adds a relaxed "roominess" field (smoothed density of unknown cells) that scales a recomputed frontier source, so the agent heads for large unknown areas (and the map edge, beyond which everything is unknown) rather than probing pockets.

70% of food spots are renewable and regrow ~1200 ticks after being eaten, but every law so far forgets a spot the moment its morsel is gone, so it only ever eats what exploration stumbles on. A larder channel remembers where morsels were seen and a per-cell harvest clock rises from 0 (just eaten) toward 1 (due), injecting the spot as a growing source as regrowth approaches; a spot found empty when due is erased, so one-shot spots are not camped. Built on #4 (ghost + confinement + roominess frontier), this turns local patches into a revisited pantry instead of a one-time find.

The agent's failure modes are dithering between two targets and re-walking ground it has already searched, and nothing in the rule knows where the agent has been. A stigmergic trail channel (laid at `here`, fading over hundreds of ticks, scrolled with the map) makes walked cells slightly less conductive to the wave, so ties and near-ties break toward fresh ground and away from backtracking, while a strong food source still pulls through a walked corridor. Built on the lingering ghost only (no confinement, no roominess), so the effect of self-avoidance is measured on its own.

Evidence: #6 (ghost + a stigmergic trail) is the only law that ever escaped world 110's sealed slot (14 meals vs 0 for every other law), while confinement + roominess (#3/#4) carry the open worlds; the observer saw the agent pace the slot pressing scattered walls. This law adds a FRUSTRATION state: accumulated dwell time, smoothed into a `crowd` field, is high only where the agent has paced for long; there it (a) multiplies the wall leak (so a taught-leaky rubble cell becomes the clear way out while learned-dead rock stays low), (b) lifts the confinement suppression, and (c) a faint pull from every unknown cell gives the wave something beyond a sealed wall to aim at. Axis: the far-vs-near trade-off. One wave gives every source the same 0.94/cell horizon, so a wide frontier ten cells away competes with a narrow one beside the agent and it zig-zags across the map instead of sweeping it. Here food (the source with the harness's 0.12 frontier marks subtracted, lingering) and exploration run as two separate waves with separate horizons — food far-sighted at 0.94/cell, exploration short-sighted at 0.85/cell — and the agent follows the larger; #7's frustration (dwell-opened walls, lifted confinement) and trail are kept as the shared conductance, so nearest-frontier sweeping is the only change.

Axis: commitment in the agent's own motion. Every law so far re-decides from scratch each thought, so near-ties between two targets or two frontiers flip the step back and forth (the trail in #6/#7 only fought this indirectly by damping walked ground). Here a fast-fading `recent` memory of the last cells walked gives each neighbour of the agent a `momentum` score (how freshly the cell opposite it, across the agent, was left), and the read-out boosts the planned value there by up to 10%: the agent keeps its heading unless another way is clearly better, which turns dithering into sweeps. The plan itself is #7's wave (frustration, roominess frontier, ghost, confinement) with the trail term remo

Axis: reading the map's geometry. The wave treats a route through never-seen cells exactly like a route over known ground, so it plans paths through unknown territory that turn out walled, and it cannot tell a doorway (a gap flanked by solid on opposite sides) from a nook, so confinement suppression also mutes the frontier at doors that open new rooms. This law adds a `gateway` field (gap detection with shift) that doubles a frontier source at a gap and exempts it from confinement, and a risk discount on cells not known free, so plans prefer known ground and exits; #7's frustration/trail/roominess substrate is kept unchanged so the geometry is the only thing under test.

The observer saw #7 on world 117 circle the outsides of small rooms full of food, pressing plain wall 42 times and opening no door: the leak is spread evenly over every solid cell, so the wave pours into thick rock as readily as into a one-cell room wall where a door can be. A `thinwall` detector (a solid cell with non-solid on both sides along an axis) keeps the taught leak only on thin walls and cuts thick rock to a third, so plans lead into room walls and doors (where the per-hue leak learning then picks the door) instead of rock masses; frustration still multiplies both, so a sealed pocket can still be dug out. Built on #10 (best untuned, 27.9), the wall-thickness rule is the one change.

Bold axis: AREA-RESTRICTED SEARCH, the classic optimal-foraging rule. Food in this world is clumped by habitat (stocked rooms hold two berries, trees two fruits, caves several mushrooms), yet every law weighs exploration the same everywhere and walks off after a meal. Here a meal (the agent beside a wanted morsel) leaves a LUCK mark pinned to that world spot (it scrolls with the map) and fading over a few hundred ticks; its PATCH (a few cells, falling off with distance) triples the frontier there and lifts confinement suppression, so the agent combs the clump — including the nooks and rooms beside it — before ranging out, and far from luck the law is #7 as before. I also drop #7's trail term

A synthesis test of the two mechanisms that each fixed a hard world without breaking another: heading momentum (#9: worlds 116/117 at 28/20 where the trail law #7 had 7/6, and still out of the world-110 pocket at 29, 20/20 immortal) and thin-wall leak (#11: world 117 6 -> 33 by leading presses into room walls instead of rock), on #7's frustration/roominess/ghost/confinement substrate — with the trail, gateway and unknown-route risk dropped (the last two are the only common factor of #10/#11's collapse to 1 meal on world 112). If momentum + thin walls are additive, the law should keep #9's floor and #11's town worlds.

Bold axis: change the PHYSICS of exploration, not its weights. Every law so far plans exploration with a max-wave, which only ever sees the single best frontier cell, so roominess had to be bolted on to say how much unknown lies beyond it. Here exploration is a HARMONIC potential — each cell takes the discounted MEAN of its neighbours (0.99*avg8, bounded: weights sum below one, no saturation cliff) clamped at frontier sources — so many frontier cells together pull harder than one crack and the field's gradient points at the mass of the unknown; food keeps its own Bellman max-wave (sources with the frontier marks subtracted, lingering), and the agent follows the larger of the two.
